comments.why: Developer sued over license server explains troll shell-company tactics
comments.text: Just watched this video [1] by someone who got sued because his "android app uses a license server". Those patent troll shell companies sue one victim after another and forward the incoming money to other companies. So there's no use in going after them directly. The victim can negotiate better terms if he signs a non-disclosure agreement. The patent trolls are protected by politicians, judges and lawyers. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: dangerlibrary
comments.story: U.S. top court tightens patent suit rules in blow to ‘patent trolls’
comments.why: Short intro to how overbroad patents hurt small tech companies
comments.text: For anyone looking for an ~20 minute intro to why this is a big deal and the impact it has on small tech companies: [VIDEO] tl;dw: There are some over-broad patents on usage of very common technologies ( using wifi or selling on the google play store are two egregious examples) that are being used as a bludgeon against small and medium sized firms that can't afford to defend themselves. It costs about $3 million to defend against such a suit, and the Eastern district is known for refusing to force plaintiffs to pay defendant's attorney's fees even if the suit is ultimately dropped.
